findings.title: The Weapons right-button heading ignores last frame's pick-up, so a right click that cancels a picked-up weapon also re-aims the MANUAL torpedo
findings.claim: Task 5's new block gates only on `(contact?.aimWeapon() ?? null) === null`. The targeting line's own listener drops a pick-up on the right press before the scene draws. So on the frame a right click cancels a picked-up LASER/TORPEDO card, aimWeapon() is already null and the block sends `torpHeading` for that same press. Decision 8 says nothing is asked while a weapon card is picked up.
findings.evidence: plan L1708 (gate is `(contact?.aimWeapon() ?? null) === null` only), plan L95-96 (Decision 8: 'Nothing is asked while a weapon card is picked up'), plan L1707 comment ('its right button cancels that'). scene.ts:162 (`lastAimed`: 'the weapon picked up on the last drawn frame (Valkyrn spec §5.1: right button)'), scene.ts:248-249 ('the targeting line's own listener has already dropped it, so the last frame's pick-up counts too'), scene.ts:253 (Flight uses `aimed: lastAimed !== null || (contact?.aimWeapon() ?? null) !== null`), scene.ts:283 (`lastAimed = aimed`).
findings.why: In ordinary play the gunner picks up a card while a MANUAL torpedo flies, then right-clicks to cancel. That right click also swings the torpedo onto an unintended held heading. Task 5's tests do not cover it.
findings.fix: Add `lastAimed === null &&` to the Weapons block's condition, as the Flight seat does: `... && lastAimed === null && (contact?.aimWeapon() ?? null) === null && onWeaponsMap(...)`. Add a scene test that picks up the laser with a MANUAL torpedo flying, sends a right press that cancels it, and expects `takeTorpHeading()` to be null.

findings.title: Task 8 Step 1's expected oracle line names <F'> = F + 4 fields, but the script prints the baseline's count; the expected arrows are '->' where the scripts print '→'
findings.claim: judgeDuelOracle prints `${was.runs[0]?.names.length} named fields`, and `was` is the Task 1 baseline. So the 'added' check prints Task 1's <F>, not <F> + 4. Every success message also uses '→'. The plan's expected lines in Task 1 Steps 4-5 and Task 8 Step 1 write '->'. An executor told to compare will see a mismatch on a passing run and may stop.
findings.evidence: plan L2605 ('`<F'>` is Task 1's `<F>` + 4: two `torpManual` and two `missiles.<k>.manual`'), plan L171, L174, L191, L2605 ('sim version 56 -> 57' / '57 -> 57'); scripts/golden/duelOracle.ts:386 (`${was.runs[0]?.names.length ?? 0} named fields ... sim version ${was.simVersion} → ${version}`); scripts/golden/versionOnly.ts:125 ('sim version ${was.simVersion} → ${now.simVersion}'); scripts/determinism/bless.ts:56 ('sim version ${from} → ${SIM_VERSION}').
findings.why: The plan is executed verbatim by fresh subagents. An expected output that cannot match a correct run invites a false stop, or teaches the executor to ignore the expected lines, which defeats the 'character for character' checks Task 8 relies on.
findings.fix: In Task 8 Step 1, expect `<R> runs, <T> ticks, <F> named fields` with Task 1's <F>, noting that the count is the baseline's. Write the arrows as '→' in Task 1 Steps 4-5 and Task 8 Step 1, or add a note that the scripts print '→'.

findings.title: The card says STEER A/D while A/D cannot steer (the 20-tick boost and the 2 s coast)
findings.claim: Decision 3 lets a MANUAL torpedo turn only while it is fuelled and past its boost. But Task 7 shows STEER A/D whenever a MANUAL torpedo flies, including ticks 1-20 and ticks 361-480, when A/D and the held heading do nothing.
findings.evidence: plan L81 (Decision 3: turns 'only while it is fuelled and past its boost (`boostTicks`, 20)'), plan L942 (`if (fuelled && m.age > def.boostTicks) ...`), plan L2537 (`weapons.torpFlyingManual === true ? 'STEER A/D' : 'FLYING'`); tuning.ts:101-102,108 (fuel 360, life 480, boost 20).
findings.why: For about a quarter of the flight the card tells the player to steer when steering is dead. It is a small feel issue, but it confuses the first owner playtest of 'is the followed torpedo easy to fly'.
findings.fix: Set `torpFlyingManual` only while `m.age > boostTicks && m.age <= fuelTicks` (or add a `torpSteerable` flag). Otherwise show FLYING, or COASTING after the fuel is spent. Alternatively, state in Decision 11 that the words are deliberately constant.

findings.title: An admitted MANUAL launch is silently skipped when the stored rock target breaks the same tick
findings.claim: A MANUAL launch leaves `torpRock` stored (Decision 4). applyWeaponsInput still skips every launch when that rock broke this call (`!(torpOnRock && s.torpRock < 0)`), but MANUAL needs no rock. The step admits the MANUAL missileLaunch as 'applied', yet nothing launches.
findings.evidence: plan L467 (MANUAL returns before touching torpRock), plan L85; weapons.ts:286 (`const torpOnRock = s.torpRock >= 0`), weapons.ts:306-310 (launch gated on the rock not breaking); step.ts:247-250 (admission via canLaunch, which in MANUAL ignores the rock).
findings.why: It is a rare edge: a rock target plus a laser burst breaking it on the tick F lands. The press reads 'applied' and does nothing, with no refusal shown.
findings.fix: Gate the skip on AUTO only, e.g. `if (s.torpManual || !(torpOnRock && s.torpRock < 0))`, which keeps AUTO unchanged. Or note it as an accepted edge in Decision 4.

findings.title: Task 8 Step 3's 'gates test unchanged' diff is vacuous if the work is done on master
findings.claim: The plan names no feature branch, and the stated worktree branch is master. `git diff --stat master -- tests/duelGates.test.ts` then compares the working tree to a HEAD that already holds every W-3 commit, so it is empty whether or not the file was edited.
findings.evidence: plan L2636 (`git diff --stat master -- tests/duelGates.test.ts`), plan L2584 ('the merge-ready branch'); the plan has no branch-creation step (no 'checkout -b' or branch name anywhere).
findings.why: The check meant to prove `tests/duelGates.test.ts` was never edited proves nothing on master.
findings.fix: Diff against the fixed base: `git diff --stat 92733195 -- tests/duelGates.test.ts`, or Task 1's parent `$(git log --grep='chore(w3): SIM_VERSION 56 -> 57' --format=%H -n 1)~1`. Or name the branch to create in Task 1.
